purpose: Solifenacin is used to treat overactive bladder (OAB). It helps reduce the sudden, strong urge to urinate, cuts down on how often you need to go to the bathroom, and can help prevent accidental leaks. It makes daily life more comfortable for people who feel like they constantly need to rush to the toilet.
how_it_works: Your bladder has muscles that can sometimes squeeze too often or at the wrong time, causing that urgent 'gotta go now' feeling. Solifenacin works by blocking certain signals in your bladder muscle called muscarinic receptors, which helps the bladder stay relaxed and hold more urine. Think of it like putting the brakes on an overactive bladder so it does not squeeze as often.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is a dry mouth, so sipping water throughout the day can help. You may also notice constipation, blurred vision, or dry eyes. Some people feel a little drowsy or have trouble fully emptying their bladder. These effects happen because the medicine relaxes smooth muscles throughout your body, not just in the bladder.
warnings: Do not take this medicine if you have difficulty urinating or a blockage in your bladder or stomach. Tell your doctor if you have glaucoma, kidney or liver problems, or heart rhythm issues, as this medication may not be safe for you. Avoid getting overheated or dehydrated since this medicine can reduce sweating. Older adults should use caution as it may cause confusion or dizziness. It can also interact with other medications, so always share your full medication list with your pharmacist.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is one 5 mg tablet taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. If needed and tolerated, your doctor may increase the dose to 10 mg once daily. Always take it around the same time each day and swallow the tablet whole. Do not crush or chew it.
